_note: The generator knows nothing about what these mean. 'name' is for humans and diagnostics only; nothing branches on it. Layer 3 reads the placement block; the height/volumetric/surface blocks are the layer 4-6 contract and are not consumed yet.
_note_bands: danger_band is roughly twice as wide as danger_preferred spacing would suggest, and that is deliberate. Narrow bands plus the quota gate leave exactly one legal biome per cell, which makes the whole assignment cost function inert -- adjacency_forbid stops being enforced and ~21% of cells fall through to the relaxation branch. Widening costs nothing measurable in quota accuracy or radial ordering. See tools/validate/README.md sections 3 and 6. The band is a legality bound; danger_preferred is what actually places a biome.
_note_caves: Caves are OFF since generator_version 11: every cave_density is 0, which skips layer 6's cave carve and, because a shaft must end in cave air, layer 7's entrances too (worldgen::caves_enabled). They were geometry nobody could reach -- residency stopped 64 m down and the shafts met cave air at 86 m. Placement is to be redesigned. The v10 values were meadows 0.25, forest 0.35, wetland 0.10, highland 0.45, badlands 0.40, taiga 0.30, ashlands 0.55, glacier 0.35, rift 0.70; cave_depth_band is untouched.
_note_trees: Layer 8. A biome's trees block is density (chance a 4 m candidate cell holds a tree, inside a patch) and cover (share of the biome's area inside a patch; the rest is clearing). Species weights are relative. A biome without a block has no trees, though its neighbours' blend weight reaches a little way across the border. Each species has an altitude band in metres: suitability ramps over 'altitude_ramp' metres inside each end, so broadleaves give way to conifers uphill and the top of the highest band is the treeline; the lower ends are all -100 so lowland trees grow full size. A tree near the end of its band is stunted. blend_sharpen raises the biome blend weights to that power for trees only, so a biome's trees keep to its own ground. form selects the engine's mesh generator; everything else under shape is presentation only and never reaches the golden hash. shape.bend is how far the wind bends the species (engine/render/tree_sway.h): 1 a broadleaf, more for a birch or a willow, less for a spruce or a dead snag.
_note_rocks: Layer 9, under the golden hash like layer 8. Two classes on their own candidate grids: boulders and outcrops. A biome's rocks block is boulders and outcrops (chance a candidate cell holds one, inside a rock patch) and cover (share of the biome inside a patch). size is metres across, skewed to the small end by a cube; sink is the share of the size set below the lowest ground under the rock (the lowest of four heights at its edge); a rock wants no steeper ground than max_slope (rise over run), and an outcrop is kept with a chance rising from 0 at slope_lo to 1 at slope_hi, so outcrops stand in slopes. Rocks keep clear of rivers, the shore, every tree trunk and (boulders) every outcrop. The engine textures each with its biome's rock_scan.
_note_detail: Layer 4's micro-relief, under the golden hash: ONE noise field shared by every biome -- period is its coarsest octave in metres, then octaves halving at gain -- which each biome scales by its own 'detail' (metres; absent is 0). Hummocks, swales and low banks below the profile's finest octave, so calm land stops reading as one smooth sheet and naturally level ground becomes rare. Scaling a shared field and blending is blending heights, never noise parameters.
_note_flats: Layer 5b, flat sites, under the golden hash: rare level ground to build on. One candidate per cell (metres), jittered inside its middle 56% so no two touch; a biome's 'flats' is the chance its candidate holds a site (absent is 0). A site's pad radius is drawn from radius; its shoulder, where the ground eases back to the terrain, is shoulder x radius but never under shoulder_min. Kept only where the land is already gentle -- no steeper than max_grade (rise over run) across the pad and out to the shoulder -- dry (shore metres above sea), and river_clear metres from any channel. The pad is pulled level to the mean of its own heights. Trees and rocks keep tree_clear metres past the shoulder, so each site is a glade.
_note_ground: Ground cover -- grass, flowers, bushes -- drawn by the engine on the GPU from the seed. Presentation only: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save, and a missing block means bare ground. grass is blade density at full patch (1 = the engine's maximum), cover the share of the biome inside a grass patch, dry how far the colour leans to dry_color, narrow 1 for reeds; flowers and bushes are chances per 1 m cell. Grass thins under a tree canopy by the same patch noise layer 8 plants trees with.
_note_materials: Terrain surface materials (ADR-004 L1), indexed by each biome's material_id. Presentation only, like ground: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save. The engine blends them per mesh vertex with the same four-cell weights layer 4 blends heights with, so a material boundary falls where the terrain's shape changes. ground is level ground -- what shows between and under the grass, so it leans the grass's way where there is grass; rock is anything steeper than about 40 degrees. Colours are sRGB-encoded, as authored; the engine linearises them. Roughness is perceptual, 0 mirror to 1 chalk. seabed is what an ocean cell's share of the blend becomes, so coasts fade to sand. ground_scan and rock_scan name CC0 scan sets in assets/textures/scans.json: the terrain shader takes their detail -- normal, roughness, occlusion, height -- and retints their albedo to the colour given here, so ground and rock set the colour and the scan the texture.
_note_fog: Mist (ADR-004 L4). Presentation only, like ground and materials: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save. A biome's fog block is the MIDDAY mist's extinction per metre at the surface (visibility is about 3.9 / density: 0.0012 is 3 km, 0.004 one km, 0.04 a hundred metres) -- morning multiplies it -- and the height in metres over which it thins by e; the engine blends them with the weights layer 4 blends heights with and bakes a map once per seed. sea_fog is the same over open water. The central, safe biomes and the sea are the misty ones on purpose: the wider map should be found, not seen. haze is a thin floor everywhere; morning multiplies the mist round dawn; the patches drift on the weather's wind (weather.mist_drift); patch is the size of the patches in metres; phase_g how forward the droplets scatter; albedo the share of light they scatter rather than absorb.
_note_weather: Weather (engine/render/weather.h): the wind every swaying thing and the sea share. Presentation only: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save. The weather is a pure function of the seed and the clock. storm is a slow noise of time with period_s (seconds); the wind speed is wind_min + (wind_max - wind_min) x storm^2, m/s; its heading wanders veer radians either side of a per-seed base over veer_period_s. The wind sea answers the wind averaged over sea_lag_s, growing as Pierson-Moskowitz but capped by fetch-limited growth over fetch_km of open water, its peak frequency times peak_shift (above 1 a younger, steeper sea than physics would grow). The swell is long waves from elsewhere: significant height swell_min to swell_max (m) from the storm averaged over swell_lag_s, around swell_wavelength (m), on a heading of its own. mist_drift is the share of the wind speed the mist's patches drift at.
_note_clouds: Volumetric clouds (docs/adr-005-clouds-and-rain.md, engine/render/clouds.h). Presentation only: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save. The weather drives them (the storm dial sets coverage, cloud type and precipitation); these shape them. base_alt is the cloud base in metres; sigma the extinction per metre at density 1; base_scale and detail_scale the tiles of the 3D noise volumes in metres (bigger is broader cloud and coarser edges); shear how far a tall cloud leans downwind at its top, metres; haze_km the e-folding distance of the fade into the horizon; detail_amount how deep the detail noise erodes the edges; drift_factor the wind aloft over the ground wind.
_note_water: The sea's body (engine/render/shaders/water.hlsl). Presentation only: nothing here reaches the golden hash or a save. extinction is per metre per channel (linear rgb): light reaching the seabed and coming back to the eye is dimmed by exp(-extinction x path), red first, which is the colour of shallow water; 0.4 / 0.11 / 0.09 is clear coastal water. deep_colour (sRGB) is what deep water sends back under the light falling on it. refraction is how far, as a share of the screen, the waves shift the seabed seen through them at full strength. storm_turbidity multiplies the extinction by 1 + itself x roughness^2 (roughness the wind over 20 m/s): a rough sea stirs up the bottom.
_note_placed_caves: Placed caves (layer 7 since v19, docs/worldgen-design.md): each biome's caves.per_km2 is a GUARANTEED density -- a jittered candidate grid of 1 km / sqrt(per_km2) cells, one cave per cell, retried at up to `tries` spots. 0 or no block = none. Built only with WorldParams::placed_caves (BIOMES_L0 caves=1) until the bump.
